subject: Commercial packaging: quantization credit split and pilot SLA request
body:
From: Jane Smith <jane.smith@finlytics.io>
To: kimberly_park@redwood.ai
Cc: 
Date: Tue, 2 Nov 2027 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Pilot packaging questions and credit allocation for Optimize Kit

Hi Kimberly,

Thanks again for the demo last week — team was impressed with the latency improvements and the analyzer dashboards. Procurement and engineering are syncing on next steps. Two quick things before we loop legal:

1) Packaging: For the 12-week pilot we talked about, Procurement prefers a split of credits: 60% inference credits (token-based) + 40% architectural credits (quantization support, batch tuning, operator time). Does Redwood have a standard template that maps credits to technical activities?

2) Quantization guidance: Engineering asks whether Redwood will support mixed precision/INT8 rollout on the Dedicated pool during the pilot, and if you can document the expected token-cost delta vs. baseline FP16. They want a conservative estimate for budgeting.

If you can send a short attachment with the recommended credit split and a one-page quantization ISR (impact, steps, rollback), Procurement can prepare a PO.

Appreciate it —
Jane
Jane Smith
Head of Procurement, FinLytics
"Message-ID: <FL-20271102-001@finlytics.io>"

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>
To: Jane Smith <jane.smith@finlytics.io>
Cc: dylan_brooks@redwood.ai, connor_obrien@redwood.ai
Date: Wed, 3 Nov 2027 11:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Pilot packaging questions and credit allocation for Optimize Kit

Hi Jane —

Thanks — and happy to put that together. Quick answers up front:

- Credit template: yes, we have a standard mapping. For pilots we typically allocate credits across: inference (tokens), ops (engineering hours for tuning), and tool credit (Optimize toolkit usage: batching/caching heuristics). I attached a pricing matrix that maps the credit categories to deliverables.

- Quantization: we support mixed-precision and INT8 profiles in Dedicated. For a conservative budgeting line, use "~25–40% token-cost reduction" vs. FP16 for typical chat-generation workloads after tuning; the range depends on prompt length and cache hit rate. We'll include a small table with example deltas for short/medium/long seqs.

Next step: I propose we offer a pilot split that allocates 55% inference credits, 30% ops credits (tuning + 2x 90-min enablement sessions), and 15% toolkit credits (Optimize features — advanced batching rules + prefix cache). This gives engineering capacity to hit the 25–40% reduction within the 12 weeks.

I'll loop Dylan and Connor to confirm the technical assumptions and the rollback plan for quantization.

Best,
Kimberly Park
Director, GTM — Optimize
Redwood Inference

Attachment: optimize-kit-pricing-matrix.xlsx (XLSX, 64KB)

From: Dylan Brooks <dylan_brooks@redwood.ai>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>, connor_obrien@redwood.ai
Cc: Jane Smith <jane.smith@finlytics.io>
Date: Thu, 4 Nov 2027 08:21:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Pilot packaging questions and credit allocation for Optimize Kit

Adding engineering notes —

Kimberly, Jane — quick technical clarifications:

- INT8 support: We can run INT8 on the Dedicated pool for the pilot. The recommended path is: baseline perf (FP16) -> conservative INT8 profile (low-bit quant for attention/FFN) -> run 1-week A/B test with live traffic mirrored to pilot variant -> evaluate quality delta on the eval set.

- Cost deltas: example conservative numbers we include in the attached PDF: short sequences (<=128 tokens) ~20–28% reduction; medium (129–512) ~28–36%; long (>512) ~35–44%. These assume a ~15–20% cache hit rate on prefix reuse. If FinLytics' workloads are high-reuse (e.g., templated prompts), expect the high end.

- Fallback & rollback: we keep FP16 snapshot and a KV-cache-compatible layout; rollback is N+1 deploy and switchover within 10 minutes if quality regression >1.5% absolute on key metrics. Ops credits in the split cover 2 on-call windows for the switch.

I'll attach a one-page ISR that summarizes steps, monitoring hooks (ROUGE/EM/LLR checks), and a short test matrix.

Dylan
Senior Research Engineer, Inference Optimizations
Redwood Inference

Attachment: quantization-profile.pdf (PDF, 28KB)

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>
To: Jane Smith <jane.smith@finlytics.io>, dylan_brooks@redwood.ai, connor_obrien@redwood.ai, marcus_lin@redwood.ai
Date: Fri, 5 Nov 2027 14:45:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Pilot packaging questions and credit allocation for Optimize Kit

Hi Jane —

Attaching the two documents (pricing matrix + ISR) and confirming our pilot offer below so Procurement can convert to a PO:

- Pilot length: 12 weeks
- Credits: 55% inference / 30% ops (tuning + 2 enablement sessions + 2 on-call windows) / 15% toolkit (Optimize advanced rules + KV-cache retention increase)
- Quantization: we will enable mixed-precision progression with INT8 candidate; conservative cost-savings estimate 25–40% (examples in PDF).
- SLA during pilot: 99.5% uptime on the Dedicated pilot pool, 95th pct latency SLO of 220ms for <=256-token requests. If we miss SLO more than twice in a month, we provide a 5% credit back applied to the pilot. (This is a pilot SLA — enterprise SLA can be negotiated post-pilot.)
- Acceptance criteria: quality regression <=1.0% absolute on the provided eval set; otherwise rollback.

If that looks good, please send the PO referencing deal FL-2027-0921 and we will kick off onboarding. Happy to set a call Monday to walk through the ISR with your engineers.

Thanks —
Kim
